_comment: The Wayfinder's keywords (game/keywords.py; design: claude/design-brisering-keywords.md). A trip is three words, one per slot, like .hack's Chaos Gates (user, 2026-11-19): danger, then land, then feature. The same three words always lead to the same place (layout fixed by the words); what's in it is rolled each trip. EVERY WORD HERE IS A PLACEHOLDER until the user writes the real vocabulary. GRAMMAR (user, 2026-11-19): danger and land words are each an adjective or a verb (pos: adjective or verb; verbs are written as -ing words, like Dancing); a place can't have a verb for both its danger and its land word (both adjectives is fine); feature words are nouns (pos: noun; a noun phrase is fine, like Victory Lap). Valid: [Hungry][Tangled][Victory Lap], [Dancing][Green][Ropeway]. Invalid: [Singing][Listing][Ideas]. Ids are lowercase; 'word' is how it's shown, in brackets. danger words: danger 1-5 (creature tiers, how rare the find is) and depth (number of areas, 1-5). land words: style (caves, ruins, forest, mountains, plains), light (day or torch: dark, torchlight only), area_size [width, height]. feature words (every key optional): light (overrides the land's), creatures (a multiplier on how many), favour (a creature id that turns up far more often, wherever it lives, if the danger allows its tier), rarity_up (the find is rolled as if the danger were this much higher), writings (a multiplier on the chance of a writing in each area). start: the words known at a new game. rank_words: words the Guild teaches a Hunter who rises to that rank (index into data/ranks.json). v0.67.0 (user, Chapter 1): Murmuring (danger 3), Specter's (caves, dark), Broken Promise (creatures halved, sight: light reaches 20% less far). Taught only by the chapter.
